samples.summary: Scope beyond the issue: a whole second concept ("heading-memory provenance" across merge and paste) was added, including a new public API export
samples.evidence: The originating task (docs/tasks/active/20260816-docs-unlist-restores-heading-todo.md) lists Steps limited to types.ts/memory.ts/yorkie-doc-store/three toggleList sites/keyboard exits, and Non-goals explicitly cover the split case. This diff additionally introduces `mergeDropsHeadingMemory` (block-helpers.ts:279), a new `pastedHeadingLevel` in text-editor.ts:42, a `removeStyleByPath` write in `YorkieDocStore.mergeBlock`, and re-exports the predicate from BOTH package entries (src/index.ts, src/node.ts) purely so the frontend CRDT store can mirror an internal invariant. It is defensible follow-on correctness, but it widens the published `@wafflebase/docs` surface for an internal rule and adds a second, inverted-looking rule (merge drops when the destination has NO text; paste drops when the destination HAS text) that future readers must reconcile.

samples.summary: Entry-export drift is fixed with a regex-over-source meta-test instead of removing the duplication structurally
samples.evidence: `blockHelperExports()` reads `src/index.ts` and `src/node.ts` as text and regex-parses `export { ... } from './store/block-helpers.js'`. The underlying design issue is that the same re-export block is hand-duplicated in two entry files; the reuse-oriented fix is a shared barrel (e.g. both entries `export * from './store/block-helpers.js'` or a common `shared-exports.ts`), which makes drift impossible rather than merely detected. The test is also brittle to formatting (double quotes, multi-line clauses, `export *`) and silently passes when it stops matching.

samples.summary: The chosen model remembers only `headingLevel`, so bulleting a Title/Subtitle is still an irreversible destruction of block type — the exact complaint the issue raises for headings
samples.evidence: `unlistedBlockType` keys off `block.headingLevel` alone, and `MemDocStore.setBlockType` only re-attaches `prevHeadingLevel`. `BlockType` includes `'title'` and `'subtitle'` (types.ts:39), which carry no `headingLevel`, so bulleting a Title and un-bulleting yields a paragraph. If the design intent is "the bullet is applied *to* the block, so leaving the list restores it", remembering the previous block type (not just a level) would cover all three; as written the invariant is heading-only and the design doc does not say why Title/Subtitle are excluded.

samples.summary: Design doc overstates "Google Docs / Word parity": the retained heading level is invisible while listed, so the user sees body text and then unexpectedly gets a heading back
samples.evidence: The new decision block says bulleting a heading applies the bullet *to* the heading "(Google Docs / Word parity)", but `blockStyleId` maps `list-item` → `normal` (packages/docs/src/model/named-styles.ts:111 default branch), so a bulleted Heading 2 renders and labels as Normal text — unlike Google Docs, where the heading formatting persists under the bullet. The doc should state that only the toggle round trip is restored and that styling-while-listed is an explicit non-goal (the todo says so; the design doc does not), otherwise the recorded rationale invites someone to "finish" the parity claim.

samples.summary: `unlistedBlockType` accepts any Block and ignores `type`, so it happily converts a paragraph that merely carries a stale level into a heading
samples.evidence: The helper only tests `block.headingLevel !== undefined`; it does not require `block.type === 'list-item'`. Its own new test asserts it on a `paragraph` input (test/view/list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts). All current call sites are guarded, but the name and signature invite calling it on arbitrary blocks; gating on `type === 'list-item'` inside the helper would make the invariant self-enforcing.
